newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish debt market edged down on Friday, as dealers said both Italian and Spanish bonds were pulled lower by renewed EMU worries.
"We have seen heavy selling since yesterday evening from international investors," a dealer in Madrid said.
Rumours on a possible election in France, and news that the European commission forecast Italy not meeting the Maastricht criteria were adding to dealers' pessimism over Europe.
"People feared again a possible delay in Europe's single currency start. Prices were pretty high -- that was a good excuse to make profits," he added.
"I would not be surprised to see the 10-year yield back to around the seven percent," a dealer said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended almost unchanged at around 109 basis points versus 110 bps this morning.
"We have to get used to shifts in mood like these ones, until the final will not be taken," a dealer added.
The peseta recovered at the close to end around 84.37/39 per mark, stronger than 84.40/42 this morning.
On the short-end of the yield curve dealers were still expecting further easing by the Bank of Spain in coming months, they added.
